cohort: The study included 76 pregnant women presenting with preterm labor, primarily primigravida aged 21-29 years.
finding: While Asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) was prevalent in 21.1% of participants, no significant associations were found between ASB and history of preterm labor, pregnancy outcomes, mode of delivery, or NICU admission.
mod_finding: No significant association was found between Asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) and mode of delivery (p = 0.872).
cross-section timing: Data was collected when pregnant women presented with preterm labor.
gest_age: The majority of participants presented with preterm labor between 33-36 weeks gestation (55.3%).
